Toussaint Louverture: Haitian general and revolutionary (1744–1803)
The only woman ever to serve as chief minister of Rajasthan, this Indian politician also held two Cabinet posts under Atal Bihari Vajpayee — who is she?

Vasundhara Raje: 11th Chief Minister of Rajasthan. Vasundhara Raje Scindia (born 8 March 1953) is an Indian politician, who has held the position of the chief minister of Rajasthan from 2003 to 2008 and 2013 to 2018.
The youngest member of China's Gang of Four, this politician organized the Shanghai People's Commune before being deposed and sentenced to life imprisonment after Mao's death — who is he?
Wang Hongwen: Chinese politician and activist (1935–1992)
Kenya's current president since 2022, he previously became the country's first elected deputy president after representing Eldoret North in parliament — who is he?

William Ruto: President of Kenya since 2022. William Kipchirchir Samoei Arap Ruto (born 21 December 1966) is a Kenyan politician who is the fifth and current president of Kenya since 13 September 2022.
A Tokyo-born artist tied to New York's Fluxus scene, she turned her 1969 honeymoon into a public protest and later recorded in the Plastic Ono Band — who is she?
Yoko Ono: Japanese artist and activist (born 1933)

Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
SQL (published 1986) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Paul Ehrenfest is a physicist. Suffering from depression, in 1933 Ehrenfest killed his disabled son, Wassik, and then himself.
What is the atomic number of Zirconium?
Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
What is the atomic number of Francium?
Francium is a chemical element; it has symbol Fr and atomic number 87.
In what year was Ursula von der Leyen born?
Ursula von der Leyen: Von der Leyen was born and raised in Brussels, Belgium, to German parents.
In what year was Factitious disorder imposed on another discovered?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
In what year was Iridium discovered?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.

Ondansetron: Pfizer. It is also effective for treating gastroenteritis.
In which country is Mitsubishi A6M Zero?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japan. It was operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) from 1940 to 1945.
Who is credited with discovering Eta Carinae?
Eta Carinae: Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser. It became the second-brightest star in the night sky between 11–14 March 1843 before fading well below naked-eye visibility after 1856.
Who is credited with discovering Benzene?
Benzene: Michael Faraday. Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
Who is credited with discovering Vanadium?
Vanadium: Andrés Manuel del Río. Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.

This mosquito species, native to tropical Southeast Asia and marked with distinctive white bands on its legs and body, has spread worldwide via international trade and travel, becoming a significant public health concern — what species is it?

Aedes albopictus (synonym Stegomyia albopicta), from the mosquito (Culicidae) family, also known as the (Asian) tiger mosquito or forest mosquito, is a species of mosquito native to the tropical and subtropical areas of Southeast Asia.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
Native to Europe but introduced to North America, this orb-weaver spider species is known by several common names, one of them shared confusingly with a different species — which species?
Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
This American physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for decisive contributions to LIGO and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish (born January 27, 1936) is an American experimental physicist and Nobel Laureate.
Despite its name, this sub-Saharan snake is actually grey to dark brown — the second-longest venomous snake in the world after the king cobra, commonly reaching 3 meters — name this species?
Black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
Also known as undulant fever and Malta fever, this zoonotic illness spreads mainly through drinking unpasteurized milk and is caused by tiny coccobacilli — what is it?
Brucellosis is a zoonosis (zoonotic disease) spread primarily via ingestion of unpasteurized milk from infected animals.
This medical specialty diagnoses and treats congenital heart defects, valvular disease, and heart failure, and is a sub-specialty of internal medicine — which field?
Cardiology (from Ancient Greek (kardi) 'heart' and - (-logia) 'study') is the study of the heart.

This compound is a yellowish-green gas above 11°C, a reddish-brown liquid when cooler, and bright orange crystals when very cold — usually handled in solution as a bleach and disinfectant. What is it?

Chlorine dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula ClO2 that exists as yellowish-green gas above 11 C (52 F), a reddish-brown liquid between 11 and 59 C (52 and 74 F), and as bright orange crystals below 59 C (74 F).
In mathematics, this term describes a selection of items from a set in which the order of choosing doesn't matter — unlike its counterpart, the permutation. Name the concept?
Combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).

Named for a mythological Greek youth who was transformed into a tree after accidentally killing a beloved stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is considered polyphyletic by modern genetic analysis — what genus is it?
Cupressus (common name cypress) is one of several genera of evergreen conifers within the family Cupressaceae; for the others, see cypress.

This is the practice of communication between representatives of states or institutions aimed at influencing international events, serving as the main instrument through which foreign policy goals are pursued. What is this practice called?
Diplomacy is the communication by representatives of state, intergovernmental, or non-governmental institutions intended to influence events in the international system.
In 2009 she became the first woman to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, honored for her analysis of how communities govern shared commons — which political economist was she?

Elinor Ostrom (ne Awan; August 7, 1933 - June 12, 2012) was an American political scientist and political economist whose work was associated with New Institutional Economics and the resurgence of political economy.
Botanists use this word for any plant whose leaves stay green and functional through every season, never going bare like a deciduous tree — what is it?
Evergreen is a plant which has foliage that remains green and functional throughout the year.
Sharing the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Maurice Wilkins, this English molecular biologist helped decipher the structure of DNA — who is he?
Francis Crick (8 June 1916 - 28 July 2004) was an English molecular biologist, biophysicist, and neuroscientist.
This pancreatic hormone kicks in when blood sugar dips too low, prompting the liver to convert stored glycogen back into glucose. What is it?
Glucagon is a peptide hormone, produced by alpha cells of the pancreas.
Newborns with this severe genetic skin disorder are born encased in thick, diamond-shaped plates separated by deep cracks that restrict movement and breathing — what is it?
Harlequin-type ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that results in thickened skin over nearly the entire body at birth.

Which field of study leans on anthropology, paleontology, and genetics to trace how our ancestors gradually picked up bipedalism, dexterity, and complex language — a story that turned out to be weblike rather than a tidy straight line?
Human evolution is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.
Denoted by the symbol ∞, this concept of the boundless and endless has been debated by philosophers since ancient Greece and by mathematicians since the 17th century — what is it?
Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
This German polymath wrote The Sorrows of Young Werther and essays on botany, anatomy, and color theory—he's the most influential writer in the German language. Who was he?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 - 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
First described in 1816 and classed in psychiatry as an impulse-control disorder, this condition is the inability to resist stealing items one doesn't even need — what's its name?
Kleptomania is the inability to resist the urge to steal items, usually for reasons other than personal use or financial gain.
Found in the support tissues of most plants, this polymer resists rot and reinforces wood and bark structure — what is it?
Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants.
This genus of Old World monkeys includes 23 species ranging from Asia and North Africa all the way to Gibraltar, and mostly eats fruit — what is it?
Macaque (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
This small southern-African mongoose has digging foreclaws and a knack for thermoregulating in harsh, dry country, living in tight packs of up to 30 — which sharp-eyed animal is it?
Meerkat (Suricata suricatta) or suricate is a small mongoose found in southern Africa.
The dried leaves of this Southeast Asian evergreen tree, known as kratom, contain alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors as partial agonists. What plant is it?
Mitragyna speciosa is a tropical evergreen tree of the Rubiaceae family native to Southeast Asia.
The paranasal sinuses all drain into this air-filled space that channels inhaled air from the nostrils down toward the throat — what is it?
Nasal cavity is an air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
This massive bony fish, weighing up to a metric ton, resembles a giant fish head without a tail and is native to tropical and temperate waters worldwide. What is it?
Ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.

Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's used in classroom and lab experiments, this single-celled ciliate thrives in freshwater, brackish, and marine habitats — what organism is it?
Paramecium ((ee-)m, -see-m, plural "paramecia" only when used as a vernacular name) is a genus of eukaryotic, unicellular ciliates, widespread in freshwater, brackish, and marine environments.
This herbaceous annual vine produces edible pods and comes in bush or climbing cultivars; global output hit 28 million tonnes in 2022, led by India. What legume species is it?
Phaseolus vulgaris is a herbaceous annual plant. Its botanical classification, along with other Phaseolus species, is as a member of the legume family, Fabaceae.

This medical condition occurs when air collects in the space between the lung and chest wall, typically causing sudden, sharp one-sided chest pain and shortness of breath — what's the condition called?
Pneumothorax is collection of air in the pleural space between the lung and the chest wall.

Named early in the history of microbiology for its widespread presence in water and plant seeds, which genus of gram-negative bacteria includes an opportunistic human pathogen infamous in hospitals as well as plant and soil-dwelling species?
Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
What fat-soluble alcohol form of vitamin A — found in fish, dairy, and meat — is essential for vision, skin maintenance, and immune function, and is used as a supplement to prevent xerophthalmia?
Retinol is a hydrolytic metabolite of retinyl esters belonging to the group of vitamin A1 as an alcohol form.

These lizard-like amphibians, grouped in the order Urodela, keep a tail throughout both their larval and adult life stages — unlike their tailless amphibian cousins the frogs and toads. What animal is it?

Salamander are a group of amphibians typically characterized by their lizard-like appearance, with slender bodies, blunt snouts, short limbs projecting at right angles to the body, and the presence of a tail in both larvae and adults.
This Pakistani-American businessman owns both an NFL franchise, the Jacksonville Jaguars, and an English Premier League club, Fulham — who is he?
Shahid Khan (born July 18, 1950) is a Pakistani and American businessman.
This circular muscle normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage, relaxing only as physiological function requires — what is it called?
Sphincter is a circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice and relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning.
Encompassing domestic pigs and their ancestor the Eurasian wild boar, this genus within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae is native across Eurasia and Africa — which genus?

Sus (genus) is the genus of domestic and wild pigs, within the even-toed ungulate family Suidae. Sus includes domestic pigs (Sus domesticus) and their ancestor, the common Eurasian wild boar (Sus scrofa), along with various other species.
A European Space Agency astronaut who is also a musician and writer, this Frenchman logged two six-month stints aboard the ISS, the second launched via SpaceX Crew Dragon in 2021 — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet (French; born 27 February 1978, is a French aerospace engineer, pilot, European Space Agency astronaut, actor, musician, and writer.
Egypt and Iraq both flew this Soviet-designed jet bomber in wars against Israel, and China still produces an updated license-built version, the H-6K — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-16 (USAF/DOD reporting name Type 39; NATO reporting name: Badger) is a twin-engined jet strategic heavy bomber used by the Soviet Union.

Belonging to the same family as kangaroos, this informally named group of smaller macropods is native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations as far away as Hawaii and the UK — what are they called?
Wallaby is a small or middle-sized macropod native to Australia and New Guinea, with introduced populations in New Zealand, Hawaii, the United Kingdom and other countries.
A white, water-insoluble powder with the formula ZnO, this compound turns up in everything from sunscreens and calamine lotion to batteries and semiconductors — name this compound?
Zinc oxide is an inorganic compound with the formula ZnO. Although it occurs naturally as the mineral zincite, most zinc oxide is produced synthetically.

First isolated from lymphoid tissue behind the nose in 1953, this family of nonenveloped DNA viruses ranges from causing the common cold to life-threatening illness in the immunocompromised — which family?
Called lucerne in the UK, Australia and New Zealand, this perennial legume has been grown as livestock fodder since ancient times — which plant?
Alfalfa: Plant species in pea family.
A member of the aminopenicillin class, this oral antibiotic is a go-to for ear infections, strep throat, and pneumonia — and is often paired with clavulanic acid. What is it?
This Soviet single-engine biplane, in production from 1947 to 2001, doubles as a crop-duster, water bomber, and paratroop transport thanks to its rugged, adaptable airframe — what is it?
Antonov An-2: Soviet single-engine civilian aircraft.
Also called the yellow-legged predatory wasp, this insect — native to parts of Southeast Asia — has become an invasive concern across much of Europe — which species?
Asian hornet: Species of insect. The Asian hornet (Vespa velutina), also known as the yellow-legged hornet or Asian predatory wasp, is a species of hornet indigenous to Southeast Asia.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?

Roughly a third of deaths from this group of over 100 diseases trace to tobacco, alcohol, obesity, poor diet and inactivity, and its malignant tumors are defined by uncontrolled cell growth that can spread — what is it?

Cancer: Group of diseases involving cell growth. Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.

This branch of metabolism breaks down large molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids into smaller units, releasing energy as cells convert the leftovers into waste like carbon dioxide and urea — what's it called?
Catabolism: Set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units.
Sometimes dubbed the 'central science' for sitting between physics and biology, this field studies how matter is composed, behaves, and transforms in reactions — what is it?
Chemistry: Scientific study of matter's behavior and properties.
Named after the French missionary who propagated it in Algeria, this citrus hybrid of mandarin and sweet orange is often sold as an 'Easy-peeler' — which fruit?
Clementine: Hybrid citrus fruit. The exterior is a deep orange colour with a smooth, glossy appearance.
Best known for its powerful, beautiful song, this small Old World flycatcher sometimes hybridizes with a closely related thrush species where their ranges overlap — which bird?
Common nightingale: Species of bird. Its range partly overlaps with that of the more northerly thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a closely related species with which hybrids have occurred.
Broken down from creatine phosphate in muscle metabolism, this compound is released into the blood at a rate tied to a person's muscle mass — what is it?
Creatinine: Breakdown product of creatine phosphate.
Also called thornapple or devil's trumpet, this genus of nine highly poisonous nightshade plants lent its American name to an outbreak in colonial Jamestown — what genus is it?
Datura: Genus of poisonous, potentially psychoactive plants.

This colourless, water-mixable lab solvent is technically odorless — but degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity. It's better known by a three-letter abbreviation; what's the compound?
Dimethylformamide: Chemical compound. Dimethylformamide, DMF is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.
This German-born British economist championed 'human-scale, appropriate technology' in his 1973 book, later ranked among the 100 most influential books since World War II — who was he?
E. F. Schumacher: British statistician and economist (1911–1977)
This messenger network of hormone feedback loops releases chemicals from internal glands like the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal glands straight into the bloodstream to regulate distant organs?
Endocrine system: Hormone-producing glands of a body.

A women's-rights campaigner schooled in 1830s New York, she was the first scientist to show certain gases trap heat — anticipating that rising CO2 could warm the climate. Who was this overlooked pioneer?
Eunice Newton Foote: American scientist and activist (1819–1888)
This genus of small-to-medium wildcats — ranging from the diminutive black-footed cat to the larger jungle cat — also includes humanity's domestic pet, the housecat — which genus?
Home to the radius and ulna joined by the interosseous membrane, this region of the arm lies between the elbow and the wrist — what is it?
Forearm: Region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.
Often triggered by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, this inflammation of the stomach lining can, in its autoimmune form, lead to pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.
Produced by the pancreas's alpha cells, this hormone raises blood sugar by triggering the liver to break down stored glycogen — the functional opposite of insulin. What is it?
Glucagon: Peptide hormone. It raises the concentration of glucose and fatty acids in the bloodstream and is considered to be the main catabolic hormone of the body.
This motorsport engineer led the Haas Formula One team from 2016 to 2023 before becoming CEO of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner: Italian and American motor racing engineer (born 1965)
Also known as the Burgundy snail and served as escargot, this large air-breathing land snail native to Europe has a globular brown shell — what species is it?
Discovered in 2013 in South Africa's Rising Star Cave system, this small-brained archaic human species yielded over 1,500 bone specimens from at least 15 individuals — which species?
Homo naledi: South African archaic human species. The initial discovery comprises 1,550 specimens of bone, representing 737 different skeletal elements, and at least 15 different individuals.

Diagnosed via Whipple's triad and most often triggered by diabetes medications like insulin, this condition causes shakiness, confusion, and sweating when blood sugar drops below 70 mg/dL — what is it?

Hypoglycemia: Decrease in blood sugar. It is defined as blood glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), symptoms associated with hypoglycemia, and resolution of symptoms when blood sugar returns to normal.
This cerebrovascular condition is a localized ballooning of a brain blood vessel most often found in the Circle of Willis, with the 'berry'-shaped type being the most common. What is it?

Intracranial aneurysm: Ballooning or rupturing of a blood vessel in the brain. The risk of rupture varies with the size and location of the aneurysm, with those in the posterior circulation being more prone to rupture.
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)
Personal physician to the Buddha and King Bimbisāra in 5th-century BCE Rājagṛha, this 'Medicine King' is still revered by traditional healers across Asia — who is he?

Jīvaka: Personal physician of the Buddha and Indian King Bimbisara. Jīvaka (Pali: Jīvaka Komārabhacca; Sanskrit: Jīvaka Kaumārabhṛtya) was the personal physician (Sanskrit: vaidya) of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisāra.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'tree of death' and 'beach apple,' this small-fruited tropical tree oozes a milky sap so toxic it can blister skin on contact — which tree?
Manchineel: Poisonous plant from tropical North and South America.

Spanning everything from sacred religious writings to the exuberantly profane, and often grouped by place, language, and genre, what broad body of European writing falls between late antiquity and the Renaissance?
Medieval literature: Literary works of the Middle Ages.
This scientific field studies microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and protists, encompassing sub-disciplines like virology and mycology — which discipline?
Ranging from a tiny 8-inch species to the 10-foot Komodo dragon, this reptile genus includes an extinct relative that may have grown over 20 feet long — what are they called?
Monitor lizard: Genus of reptiles. Monitor lizards are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
This Danish physicist won the 1922 Nobel Prize for a model of the atom in which electrons leap between discrete, stable orbits around the nucleus — who is he?
Native to East Africa and known in some places as 'lady's fingers,' this mallow-family plant is prized for its edible green (sometimes red) seed pods — what is it?
Prized both as a delicacy and, in some species, for the pearls grown within its shell, which salt-water bivalve is this?
Oyster: Variety of families of Mollusca.
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.
This beta blocker treats high blood pressure and performance anxiety alike, and can even shrink capillary hemangiomas in infants — what drug?
Propranolol: Beta blocker drug. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.
First identified in the 1950s as a radio source, this extremely luminous galactic nucleus can outshine an entire galaxy like the Milky Way thousands of times over — what is it?
Quasar: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) containing a supermassive black hole.
Often compared to the film in a camera, this innermost, light-sensitive layer of the eye sends signals along the optic nerve to the visual cortex — what is it?
Retina: Part of the eye. The retina (from Latin rete 'net'; pl. retinae or retinas) is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrograph images, this fecal-oral pathogen is the leading cause of diarrheal illness in infants worldwide — which pathogen?
Rotavirus: Specific genus of RNA viruses.
Found in every ocean but never in fresh water, most of these bivalves can swim in rapid bursts across the seafloor rather than staying put — which shellfish?
Scallop: Family of shellfish, many edible.
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.
A hygroscopic crystalline powder (formula NaNO2) and the most industrially important salt of its kind, this compound is most familiar to us cured into processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite: Chemical compound. It is a white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder that is very soluble in water and is hygroscopic.
Famous for kite-shaped plates along its back and spikes on its tail, this Late Jurassic herbivore may have been preyed on by Allosaurus — which dinosaur?
Stegosaurus: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur.
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
The primary male sex hormone, this androgen builds muscle and bone, spurs body hair, and is even linked to mood, courtship display and dominance in both sexes — what is it?
Testosterone: Primary male sex hormone. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
One of only a few fish able to keep its body warmer than the surrounding water, this fast-swimming ocean predator's yellowfin members can reach 75 km/h — what is it?
Tuna: Tribe of fish. Tuna (pl.: tunas or tuna) is a saltwater fish that belongs to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the Scombridae (mackerel) family.
This abnormal enlargement of veins in the scrotum is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, affecting around 15% of all men — what is it called?
Varicocele: Abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform plexus veins in the scrotum.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.
This Egyptian archaeologist twice served as his country's Minister of Tourism and Antiquities and has dug at sites from the Nile Delta to the Western Desert — who is he?
What is the chemical symbol for bromine?
The symbol for bromine is Br. Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Tantalum is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tantalum is Ta. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.

In what year was Sarah Michelle Gellar born?
